title: IX_Orders_CustomerId_Wide: 20 included columns, 37.9 GB
prompt: Azure SQL Database 'RetailOps', General Purpose, 8 vCores, about 41.5 GB of memory, compatibility level 160, no readable secondary. Snapshot taken Thursday 2026-09-24 09:00 UTC. A platform failover reset the index usage counters on 2026-09-15 02:41, so they cover 9.26 days. Query Store holds data from 2026-09-11 only, because size-based cleanup has run. Month-end change freeze: 2026-09-30 18:00 to 2026-10-02 18:00. Flash sale on 2026-10-09 with a change freeze from 2026-10-08. Log rate cap: 36 MB/s. Space headroom: 213 GB.
IX_Orders_CustomerId_Wide has 99,100 seeks in nine days. Someone proposes to keep it 'because it is used'. Assume the
two (CustomerId, OrderDate) indexes have already been merged into IX_Orders_CustomerId_OrderDate with INCLUDE
(Status, TotalAmount, CurrencyCode, ChannelId), and that the October month-end run has finished. Decide.

workload.sql: SELECT TOP (20) o.OrderId, o.OrderDate, o.Status, o.TotalAmount FROM dbo.Orders o WHERE o.CustomerId = @CustomerId ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC;
workload.plan: Index Seek (backward) IX_Orders_CustomerId_OrderDate, then Top. Plan 88213 is forced in Query Store since 2026-06-14; force_failure_count 0.

sql: SELECT TOP (50) o.OrderId, o.OrderDate, o.Status, o.ChannelId, o.ExternalOrderRef, o.WarehouseId, o.TotalAmount,
o.CurrencyCode, o.ShipMethod, o.ShippingName, o.ShippingPostCode, o.PromisedShipDate, o.Notes
FROM dbo.Orders o WHERE o.CustomerId = @CustomerId ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC;
workload.plan: Index Seek IX_Orders_CustomerId_Wide (CustomerId = @CustomerId), then Top N Sort.

workload.sql: UPDATE dbo.Orders SET Status = @Status, UpdatedAt = SYSUTCDATETIME() WHERE OrderId = @OrderId;
workload.plan: Maintains IX_Orders_CustomerId_OrderDate, IX_Orders_CustomerId_Wide, IX_Orders_Status and IX_Orders_ChannelId_UpdatedAt.

facts: dbo.Orders: 182M rows, 350k inserts a day, about 2.1M status updates a day, 340k invoice updates a day.
IX_Orders_CustomerId_Wide: 26.3M updates and 1.94M page splits in the window; fragmentation 38%. Every status update (Q7) maintains it.

Q3 is its only reader: TOP (50) ORDER BY OrderDate DESC for one customer. Through the wide index it reads the customer's whole range and sorts. Through (CustomerId, OrderDate) it is a backward ordered seek with at most 50 key lookups, about 200 reads.
The largest business customer has 31k orders. The customer-service screen cannot open the shared guest account.

Incident on 2026-06-14: after a statistics update the optimizer chose this index and a Top N Sort for Q1; business customers took 40 s and CPU sat at 100% for 40 minutes. Plan 88213 was forced to stop it.
The weekly maintenance job rebuilds this index; that job generated 131 GB of log on 2026-09-20.

decisions.why: Its one reader is served better by the (CustomerId, OrderDate) index. It is the most expensive index to maintain on the table and the cause of a past incident. Saves about 38 GB.
It serves Q1, with a forced plan, and takes over Q3.

must_not_create.why: A replacement index on CustomerId alone, covering or not, repeats the Top N Sort plan.

harmful_removals.why: Q1 runs 430,000 times a day on it, and its forced plan would start to fail.
